text: A lock ratified by hand holds only for the exact proposal a person ratified, as a lock ratified on GitHub holds only for the hash its comment names. `invariant decisions ratify -by @PERSON -proposal sha256:… ID` records that proposal on the ratify line, the only line of a decision's journal that may name one. A lock that names a decision and no ratifying comment holds only when the repository's journal holds that decision, nothing has superseded it, and a person ratified it on a ratify line of their own that names exactly the lock's ProposalHash; a decision recorded as ratified when it was decided holds no lock, whoever wrote it down. CI's ratification check holds every such lock to this, and so does `invariant decisions check`, which reads only the checkout and runs on every change. The gate fails such a lock that isn't what was ratified, in a repository that keeps a journal, and its receipt names the decision and the person; the dashboard counts it among the factory locks it checked. The journal records that a person ratified, as it records every decision: CI checks the record, and can't prove the person made it, as it can a comment on GitHub. D-0202 and D-0203 were each ratified once, with no proposal named, so two new decisions ratify their locks' exact proposals.
